Fourteenth pre-release for the 0.15.0 test pass, superseding v0.15.0-dev13. Everything below lands in v0.15.0 once it survives - install this only to help catch what didn't.

### Highlights

- **Antennas** (#111) - a dedicated antenna component and device-type template with structured RF fields: numeric gain in dBi, multi-select bands, polarization, RF connector, direct-mount flag. RF connector types (RP-SMA, SMA, N-type, MMCX, U.FL, QMA, 4.3-10) join the aux-port vocabulary, so an AP to external antenna coax run is an ordinary cable between RF ports. Antennas get their own pane on the device Hardware tab, ride along in bundle export/import, and faceplates draw RF slugs as antenna stubs.
- **Circuit terminations cable like ports** (#118) - the provider handoff cables to the switch port it lands on, with a Device/Circuit toggle on each cable end. Traces and the device Paths tab run out to the demarc and show the circuit as a link.
- **Interface lifecycle status** (#105) - Active / Disabled / Planned / Not present / Decommissioning on every interface, set by SNMP sync where it applies, respected by utilization and monitoring, with bulk edit and filters.
- **Sync a device type's whole fleet** (#103) - preview, a warning step that counts what gets removed (red when interfaces carrying IPs are among it), then a background run with progress and per-device permission re-checks.
- **GeoJSON / QGIS boundary import** (#80) - upload a region boundary; WGS84 is enforced (projected exports are refused with a reproject hint), multi-feature files merge, and Douglas-Peucker simplification trims the shape until it fits - with a report of what that cost.
- **Every edit form on the sectioned card layout** (#78) - two columns where they earn them, colored pickers everywhere a table shows a badge, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter saves, and dialogs grow to fit their content instead of scrolling sideways.

### New since dev13

- **Stack-wide port utilization** - the virtual chassis page carries the device page's utilization card summed over every member (`/api/virtual-chassis/<id>/port-utilization/`).
- **Photo-port hover shows the VLAN** - the hover card on a photo port now carries the same rows as the drawn faceplate's (name and printed label, type, state, VLAN with its badge, live SNMP state, IPs) in the order set under Settings → Components.

### New since dev12

- **Lit marked ports draw in their speed tier** - with *Light up ports marked connected* on, a marked port was drawn in the free grey and read as unlit; faceplates and photo ports now paint it like a cabled port of that speed.

### New since dev11

- **Custom-field values are searchable** - every search bar (the global one and each list's filter box) matches inside custom fields, so an imported NetBox id (`57` for what was `/cables/57/`) finds its object.
- **Custom-field definitions can be hidden** - the value stays on the object and in search, but no card, table, popover or form shows it. The NetBox importer creates its `netbox_id` / `netbox_tenant` definitions hidden by default. Migration `customization.0006`.
- **Faceplates can light up ports marked connected** - a deployment setting (Settings → Admin → Faceplates, off by default) makes drawn faceplates and photo panels draw a port with an undocumented cable like a cabled one. Migration `core.0046`.

### New since dev10

- **Speeds given as bare kbps read as the dropdown's form** - a scraper writing `1000000` now lands as `1G` (`25000000` → `25G`, `100000` → `100M`, `1234000` → `1.234G`) on save through the API, the form, bulk edit and VM interfaces; anything with a unit is kept as typed. The parser behind SNMP drift and LAG capacity reads bare numbers as kbps too. Migration `api.0154` rewrites rows already stored that way.

### New since dev9

- **Floor plans clone** - a Clone action on the floor plans list copies a plan with everything drawn on it (tiles with their rack / device links, trays without their cable assignments, raised-floor areas, walls) into the same location as `<name> copy` and opens it.
- **Floor plan tiles** - a placed tile's type or role can be changed from the inspector without re-placing it; the tile popover shows the uploaded front / rear photo when that side has no ports mapped (the mapped photo when it has, the drawn panel only without a picture) and lays its rows out striped like the site map's inspector; Faceplate is on by default in the popover.
- **Show on floor plan zooms in** - the button on the rack and device pages opens the plan zoomed onto the tile; an object placed on several plans gets a menu listing them.

### New since dev8

- **Photo panels at the right size** - the device page's photo panel drew the picture at the column's full width (a portrait shot came out enormous). It now draws at the upload size, capped to the pane, or - tick **Use this size everywhere** in the photo-port editor - at the Fit / zoom saved with that side's layout. Nothing changes for existing types until someone opts in.
- **Virtual chassis** - the edit form has a Tags field (the model and API always had them), and the list's sidebar gains a Status facet: a stack whose members agree shows as that status with its colour, a mixed stack lists the distinct ones, and the badge in the row filters like a tag.
- **Virtual topology** - the diagram scrolls inside a viewport-high box, so its horizontal scrollbar is on screen instead of below a page-high drawing.

### New since dev7

- **Link aggregation done right** (#145) - an aggregate is an interface of type LAG carrying the bundle settings: protocol (static / LACP / PAgP), LACP mode and rate, min links. Members may sit on any member of the same virtual chassis, so a stack's port-channel lives once on the master. The LAG picker offers aggregates only, with an inline "New aggregate"; the interface table gains a LAG column (member to its aggregate, aggregate to its link count); the aggregate's page has a Bundle card (capacity, peer aggregates, min-links verdict), a Members tab and its members' cable runs; a member's page carries a "Member of Po1 · LACP active" chip; the device overview groups a bundle's runs under it; topology folds a bundle's member cables into one thick edge (Display → Bundle aggregates, `?lag=off` to see every cable). SNMP discovery reads membership (LAG-MIB, ifStackTable fallback), creates aggregates typed LAG and reports `lag_membership` drift; sync applies it. Migrations `api.0152`, `api.0153` (promotes untyped aggregates that already have members to type LAG).
- **IP ranges as allocation pools** (#143) - adding an IP inside a subnet that holds ranges offers a Range field; picking one shows what's free, one-click picks, a Next free button, and a nudge when the typed address falls outside the span. The range page's Addresses tab is the ordinary IP table cut to the span, free rows click-to-add, with a Compact fold ("first free · N more") that the prefix IPs tab has too.
- **Tables: badges sort and filter on click** - Status / VLAN / role headers sort on every table, sort headers show their direction, and a tag chip or an enum badge (status, family, DHCP, zone…) in a cell toggles that filter in the rail, just like ticking it there - links keep navigating. The prefix IPs rail draws its facets with the shared badge instead of a dot.
- **Site edit page stopped wiping engine / SNMP bindings on reload** (#125, second cause) - browser and extension autofill fires change events on a form's hidden native selects, which the save-on-change binding controls persisted as real changes; changes without a user gesture are now ignored, no-op changes skipped, and the controls stay disabled until loaded. Also: an RBAC constraint that doesn't fit the model fails closed instead of 500ing.
- **SNMP source-of-truth policies** - update-only (never add interfaces), skip unrouted L2 VLAN rows, take the MAC from the forwarding table; grouped-VLAN VID matching; a default VRF for discovered addresses per device / role / type / site / tenant. Migrations `monitoring.0079`–`0081`.
- **Photo ports per device, printed labels, stable markers** - a device can override its type's photo-port layout (Photo ports tab, Reset to type layout); interfaces and front/rear ports carry a printed label shown in tables, hovers and traces; ports keep a frozen marker identity so renaming a port never orphans its photo marker; the editor fits the image and zooms. Migrations `api.0148`–`0151`.
- **Trace, sidebar, docs** - trace segments make room for the link-icon glyph; the sidebar nav sits tighter with a per-category rail; Docker docs gain a front-nginx example and WebSocket troubleshooting (#146).

### New since dev6

- **Clicking a MAC no longer 500s on VM-polling tenants** (#139) - the sighting walker assumed every SNMP state row belonged to a device, but VM rows carry no device; sightings now name the device or the VM, and a MAC learned in a VM's ARP/FDB table shows on the MAC page.
- **VM interfaces nest** - pick a Parent interface (same VM, loops refused) and `wg0` rides under `eth0`; the table indents children beneath their parent. Migration `api.0147`.

### New since dev5

- **Site SNMP settings display for site-scoped users** (#125) - the binding saved but the profile catalog list was still refused, so the select rendered empty and read as not saved; a picker-options endpoint (id/name/version, no secrets) now serves anyone who may set a binding.
- **VM interfaces get a type** (#140) - Virtual (default), Tunnel (WireGuard/GRE/VXLAN/tun), Bridge, or Loopback; the form drops MAC/speed for tunnels and loopbacks, the table shows the type. Migration `api.0146`.

### New since dev4

- **Fixed the stray text on the device Components tab** - a code comment shipped in dev3/dev4 rendered at the top of the pane and squeezed it to half width.
- **Renaming a component template follows into photo markers** - photo ports and custom faceplate slots reference templates by name; a rename no longer orphans the placed port (all markable kinds).
- **The rack Assign dialog places half-width devices** - picking a half-width type reveals a Left/Right half choice; the Assign path could not place them before.

### New since dev3

- **Virtual chassis list shows combined status and monitoring** - the members' lifecycle statuses as one badge when they all agree or a racing-flag split of the distinct colors when they don't, plus a merged monitoring rollup across every member's checks; one bulk request per page.

### New since dev2

- **Device pages stay inside the viewport** (#132) - the Components pane contained its widest table instead of growing the whole page sideways on laptop widths; tables scroll in their own containers and the sub-tab bar keeps its actions pinned.
- **IP form keeps your subnet** - picking a prefix and then narrowing to its own site no longer clears it (filters only clear a subnet they actually exclude), and adding an IP from a device/VM interface pre-selects the target's site (#135).
- **Interface VLAN pickers put the device's site first** (#136) - site VLANs float to the top of the untagged picker and sort first in the trunk checklist; shared VLANs stay reachable.
- **Aggregate pages list their prefixes** (#133) - a Prefixes tab with the count in its title, backed by a new `contained_in=<cidr>` prefix filter.
- **Add device from a site** (#134) - the site's Devices tab opens the device form with the site pre-filled.
- **Disconnect a cable from the interface list** (#137) - an unplug action beside Trace on cabled rows, confirm names both ends.
- **Rack-face images get a visible Resize control** - each face shows its pixel size and a Resize menu (1600/1200/800 px) that re-encodes in place, aspect preserved.
- **Short ids are searchable** - an all-digit query matches the number printed on labels across every searchable type, and cables join global search (label text or short id).
- **Cable labels get bare port names** - `a_port_name` / `b_port_name` tokens for short labels.
- **Virtual chassis members show live monitoring** - the check rollup badge sits next to each member's status pill in the Members table and the stack drawing; the Overview card also carries the stack's primary and OOB IPs.
- **Search puts the closest match first** (#138) - the IP list ranks exact, then prefix, then substring (typing .13 no longer buries it under .130-.139), and every combobox now scores matches the same way instead of keeping raw list order.
- **The assign-IP picker flags taken addresses** - an already-assigned IP greys out and names where it lives (interface, device, or VM); still selectable, since assigning deliberately moves it.

### New since dev1

- **Poll now routes through the site's Outpost** (#128) - a device on an Outpost-bound site queues its manual SNMP poll on that Outpost (answering *Queued on Outpost ...*) instead of polling centrally and reporting outpost-only networks unreachable; the agent runs its cycle on the next pass. The Outpost-offline window is also configurable per tenant (#129): **Outpost offline after N minutes**, 0 = the automatic 3x poll rule.
- **Circuit terminations show the cabled switch port** (#118) - a device port cabled to a circuit end now appears on the circuit page's termination card as *Cabled to*.
- **Cable form port panel** (#130) - long interface prefixes truncate with a hover reveal instead of running into the next group, and the panel gets a per-browser Hide toggle.
- **Custom fields render as cards in the new forms** - each custom-field group is its own card section; a group flagged collapsed opens itself when it holds values.
- **Enabling Match existing VLANs migrates old networks** - a network that minted its own VLAN before the toggle is re-pointed at the matching real VLAN on the next sync (hypervisor name kept, NICs follow); hand-assigned VLANs are never touched.
- **Device photos downscale on upload** - device-type faces, library fetches, and image attachments cap at 2000px on the longest edge, aspect preserved, EXIF rotation applied.
- **Device-type documents carry to every device** - a manual attached on the type's new Documents tab shows read-only on each device under *From device type*.

### Records & IPAM

- **Working hours on contacts** (#66) and **provider support details** (#67) - a shared weekly schedule (multiple spans per day, time zone required), an "Open now" readout, and provider fields for support contract, support phone, and an account manager.
- **SSID pre-shared keys live in the secret store** (#68) - write-only on the form, revealed only through a separate audited action behind its own grant, fail-closed when no store is configured.
- **VM primary IP from the address form** (#122), VLAN prefixes assignable straight from the VLAN page, site time zone as a dropdown (#120), searchable custom-field rule pickers (#113), custom fields on 12 more detail pages (#114), restored Add/Import buttons (#112).
- **Name ranges expand server-side** - `eth[1-4]` fans out in one request on ports, templates, and components alike, atomically: one clash fails the whole range before anything is created.

### Access & sign-in

- **Hide local login behind a link** (#119) - SSO buttons lead; "sign in with a local account" reveals the form, `/login?local=1` deep-links it, and the page fails open when no provider is enabled.
- **grant_superuser as a permission verb** - a user-admin can set or clear superuser without being one: unscoped grants only, flag-only edits on superuser targets, the same gate on SSO mappings that mint superusers, every flip audited.
- **A tenant-scoped grant is tenant access** - users reach tenants named on their grants (directly or via a group) without a second manual membership step.

### Floor plans & 3D

- **Faceplate popovers** (#102) - a device-linked tile can draw the box's front/rear panel in its hover popover.
- **Tiles redrawn** - a seam between adjacent tiles, calmer outlines, linked tiles filling heavier than planning ghosts, and the facing indicator moved inside the tile where it can't bleed into the neighbour.
- **3D device labels** - devices placed on the map carry a camera-facing name tag above their massing, named like the 2D canvas names them.
- **3D walls no longer vanish** - switching shell mode and render quality could leave walls invisible until a lucky toggle brought them back (an in-place material swap corrupted its transparency flags); x-ray walls also render visibly on the dark theme now.

### Monitoring & integrations

- **Monitoring settings get their own tab** (#63), and switch-link suggestion ARP sources actually persist (#127) - picked sources also show their device name immediately, dashed until saved.
- **Windows DHCP lease sync survives non-MAC ClientIds** (#115) - a DUID or RFC 4361 id no longer aborts the scope.
- **Virt sync can match existing VLANs by ID** (#116) - opt-in per source; a tagged network resolves to the tenant's own VLAN before minting one.
- **Adopted VMs surface spec drift** - a hypervisor re-size queues a review row for operator-owned VMs instead of auto-applying.
- **Site SNMP binding accepts a site grant** (#125) - it used to demand an unconstrained device grant and silently snap the select back.

### Everyday interface

- **Every page names its browser tab** - settings sections, dashboards, topology, floor plans, planning boards, jobs, and the rest; object pages use the loaded name.
- **The sidebar shows where you are** - a primary bar on the active group's band and a rail down the cluster holding the current page; floor-plan sidebar rows show the linked device's name under the label, and search matches it.
- **Circuit install/termination dates use the calendar picker**, long select values truncate with a hover reveal (#124), tooltips stopped inverting in dark mode, the advanced filter's value list scrolls (#117), docs links survive a missing trailing slash (#123).
- Change-log filters survive back navigation (#109), saved views split from the Devices list (#107), the site map can't be squeezed to nothing (#108), serializers that override validate() no longer skip base validation (#106).

### Upgrading

Migrations cover the interface status seed, antennas, business hours, SSID PSK references, hide-local-login, VLAN matching, the circuit-termination cable point, and device-type run kinds - they apply automatically. The #123 docs-redirect fix (`proxy_redirect / /docs/;`) only reaches existing installs when their nginx config is regenerated or patched by hand.
